svg.title: Fork, redirect, exec, and publish only after success
svg.desc: A host Linux process trace. Fork makes two processes with separate descriptor tables. In child 202, open returns 3; dup2 makes descriptors 0 and 3 refer to the same open file description A with one offset. Closing 3 leaves 0 connected. Exec replaces the child program while its PID and descriptor 0 survive. The parent waits for exactly child 202. Only a matching returned PID and stored status zero let the controller rename unit.o to the unit object path.
svg.text: Replace the program. Keep the input.
One successful compile-unit call on host Linux
Assume fd 0/1/2 open (not close-on-exec); child open → 3.
Separate tables; inherited open-file descriptions are shared.
Two descriptors. One stream and one shared offset.
Same process. Fresh program. Input binding survives.
Only now can the parent publish it.
Manual, source-derived trace · execution order within lanes; no Linux scheduling order assumed
